Here's your permit path for a **pushcart without cooking** (like ice cream or packaged food). Good news: it's the lightest route — no DMV registration and no fire permit for most no-heat carts.

You'll deal with **four city bodies, in this order**: the Treasurer (business registration), Public Health (food safety), Public Works (your location permit), and — only if you add heat later — the Fire Department.

The clocks to watch: the **30-day public notice** after you apply for the location permit, the **90-day window** to gather your documents, and the **15-day appeal window** after a decision.

One heads-up that surprises people: you'll need a **restroom agreement** — a business within 200 feet must sign a letter letting your staff use their restroom.

Work the checklist below top to bottom. And to be straight with you: this is a guide to the process, not legal clearance — confirm the final details with the SF Permit Center before you spend money.

citations.label: DPW Order 182,101 §2 — MFF permit requirements
citations.quote: No person shall maintain or operate a Mobile Food Facility on any public street... without first obtaining a permit from the Department of Public Works.

citations.label: DPW Order 182,101 §4 — public notice period
citations.quote: Upon submission of a complete application, the Department shall post notice at the proposed location for a period of thirty (30) days.

citations.label: Vendor-type checklist — pushcart (no cooking)
citations.quote: Push carts that do not cook, heat, or hold hot food are exempt from Fire Department permit requirements and DMV registration.

steps.title: Register your business
steps.detail: Get a Business Account Number (BAN) online. Free for small businesses under the SF gross receipts threshold. You need this number for every other application.

steps.title: Get a food handler / manager card
steps.detail: At least one person needs a Food Safety Manager certificate; everyone else handling food needs a California Food Handler card (online course, same day).

steps.title: Apply for your Mobile Food Facility health permit
steps.detail: Submit cart plans/spec sheet to DPH Environmental Health. A no-cook cart has the lightest review — no hood, no grease, no water heater requirements.

steps.title: Line up your commissary
steps.detail: Even a packaged-goods cart must be stored and serviced at a permitted commissary. Get the commissary agreement letter signed — DPH will ask for it.

steps.title: Pick your location(s) and check clearances
steps.detail: Pushcarts need wider sidewalk clearance than trucks — keep a clear pedestrian path. Check the 75 ft restaurant-entrance rule and school buffers before you apply. Use the map side of this app to test a spot.

steps.title: Get your restroom agreement signed
steps.detail: A business within 200 ft of your spot must sign a letter allowing your staff to use their restroom during operating hours. Bring this with your application.

steps.title: Submit your MFF location permit application
steps.detail: File with DPW including site plan, health permit proof, commissary letter, and restroom agreement. You have a 90-day window to complete the document package once you start.

steps.title: Wait out the 30-day public notice
steps.detail: DPW posts notice at your proposed location for 30 days. Neighbors can object during this period — have a backup spot in mind in case one draws protests.

steps.title: Decision + appeal window
steps.detail: After the notice period, DPW approves or denies. Either side has 15 days to appeal. If approved with no appeal, you pay the permit fee and get your location permit.

steps.title: Fire permit — not needed (no cooking)
steps.detail: A cart with no cooking, heating, or open flame doesn't need an SFFD permit. If you ever add a hot-food element (coffee urns, warmers), come back to this step.
